title: A várható élettartam jövedelmi egyenlőtlenségei Magyarországon 1992–1993 és 2022–2023 között
summary_en: Hungary's life-expectancy gap by income widened sharply over the post-1990 decades. Bíró, Kertesi and Hajdú trace the income-gradient in life expectancy in Hungary from 1992–93 to 2022 using administrative income-and-mortality data, and document a substantial widening of the gap between top and bottom income deciles, consistent with parallel patterns in the US and the UK. The chapter pinpoints which mortality causes drive the gap and how it has evolved across age groups and over time.
policy_relevance: Direct relevance for Hungarian health policy (EMMI, NEAK, NNK) and inequality monitoring (KSH equity dashboards): the income-gradient in life expectancy is a headline indicator of system-wide inequality outcomes. Suggests Hungarian health spending should be evaluated not only on average outcomes but on the bottom-decile mortality reduction. Useful input for the Hungarian health-strategy refresh and for Belügyminisztérium poverty-reduction targets.
